<question>
I signed a rental contract in Spain on 1 March 2024 with a landlord who is a private individual, and his agent charged me the agency's fee. On that date, could the fee be put on me?
</question>

<answer>
No. On 1 March 2024 the last sentence of article 20.1 of the Ley de Arrendamientos Urbanos said that property-management and contract-formalisation costs are the landlord's, whoever he is [1]. That rule depended on the landlord being a legal person until Ley 12/2023 took effect on 26 May 2023, and it no longer does [1].

A tenant who has already paid such a fee may recover the amount from the landlord as an overpayment of costs under the contract [1].
</answer>

<reference>
No. On 1 March 2024 the last sentence of art. 20.1 of the Ley de Arrendamientos Urbanos said that property-management and contract-formalisation costs are the landlord's, whoever he is; the rule, which depended on the landlord being a legal person until Ley 12/2023 took effect on 26 May 2023, no longer does.
</reference>

In your reasoning, name the rule the reference states, then say whether the answer states it, leaves part of it out, or contradicts it.

The answer states the same conclusion ('No'), the same article and sentence, the same whoever-he-is principle, and the same Ley 12/2023 / 26 May 2023 timing.
